summary: Weekly POC sync focused on investigating recent prompt regressions and defining a short stability gate. Team reviewed scorecard drift, discussed possible causes (model variant switch, tokenization edge cases, KV cache priming), and agreed experiments to triage. Action items assigned for trimmed prompt set, targeted tests, and a brief Dedicated vs Hosted comparison pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-14 16:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Sofia (Redwood) — Carlos, Priya, Liam, Naomi (Meridian)

Summary (auto): quick triage of recent regressions; define gating experiments and owners.

[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, short agenda today: quick scorecard review, triage root causes, decide on stability gate experiments, and confirm next steps.
[00:18] Carlos (Head of AI): thanks Maya. we've seen a bump in failure rate last week, about 6.2% to 9.9% on our customer-facing intents. some of these look like hallucination-ish, others are formatting breaks.
[00:30] Jonah (SE): got it. we pulled the per-prompt heatmap — I uploaded a quick sheet (link in chat) — there are clusters around longer context prompts and a handful of short prompts with specific named entities.
[00:45] Priya (ML): yeah, the short named-entity prompts are weird because they used to be fine; we didn't change prompts. the only infra change was the model bumped from v1.2 to v1.3 last Tuesday.
[01:10] Sofia (SE): v1.3 included a tokenizer tweak, likely tokenization edge-case. sometimes punctuation normalization can change prefix matching which affects the KV cache hits.
[01:30] Liam (Platform): we also changed our request batching window slightly to improve throughput in peak — small change but could impact latency distribution.
[01:45] Noah (Speaker 1)?: (inaudible)
[02:00] Maya: ok, so hypothesis list: 1) model variant change (v1.2->v1.3) caused behavior delta, 2) tokenization adjustment breaks some exact-match guards, 3) cache priming not happening on shorter prompts due to batching. any other ideas?
[02:20] Carlos: also want to consider that our reranker threshold was lowered two weeks ago, could be more permissive and letting lower-fidelity outputs through.
[02:35] Jonah: good point. also -- I want to test whether Redwood's prefix caching is evicting earlier than expected under your traffic profile. we can instrument cache hit rates and compare.
[02:50] Priya: how invasive are the cache logs? we need to keep PII filtered.
[03:05] Sofia: we have redaction hooks; we can send aggregated cache metrics rather than raw tokens. we'll mark PII fields before logs leave your VPC. (brief chuckle)
[03:25] Maya: noted. quick check on the scorecard: for the last 7 days the F1 on intent classification fell from 0.88 to 0.81, and user-facing formatting errors rose 3x.
[03:45] Carlos: that matches our dashboard. the business impact is: support tickets up, and some SLA breaches for our enterprise accounts. so this is high priority.
[04:00] Jonah: proposal for stability gate: pick a 120-prompt trimmed set (high-priority + known edge cases). run three experiments in parallel: A) pinned model v1.2 baseline, B) v1.3 with cache disabled, C) v1.3 with cache enabled + priming. measure pass rate, latency p95, cost per 1k tokens and reranker delta.
[04:25] Maya: and add D) a quantized variant to quickly estimate cost/latency changes?
[04:30] Jonah: yes, but quantized run might change behavior — we should treat it as exploratory.
[04:40] Priya: for scoring, can we lock the same reranker? we want to ensure comparisons are apple-to-apple.
[04:50] Maya: agree, reranker threshold will be fixed for tests.
[05:00] Naomi (Product): what about guardrails? some of the failures were guardrail bypasses. are we missing a normalization step?
[05:12] Jonah: likely tokenization plus prompt formatting. e.g., a trailing newline changed classifier signals. We'll add normalization in the test harness.
[05:30] Carlos: also request tracing. we need to see which model variant served each request in our logs.
[05:40] Liam: we can annotate telemetry with model_id and route, no problem.
[05:48] Maya: ok timeline idea: Maya sends trimmed prompt set and scoring rubric by Friday (10/17). Meridian annotates top-12 failure cases by Thursday (10/16). Jonah runs experiments and returns results by Monday (10/20).
[06:05] Priya: can you run a quick deterministic rerun for the 12 failures? we want to reproduce.
[06:15] Jonah: yes, deterministic seeds and same model_param config — we'll do that first.
[06:25] Maya: short digression — cost vs latency: if Dedicated reduces p95 by 40% our cost delta might be +12% but the SLA benefit could justify it.
[06:40] Carlos: we need concrete numbers. can you do a side-by-side estimate?
[06:50] Maya: yes, we'll run a conservative estimate and a measured 1-week micro pilot if needed.
[07:00] Sofia: note on tooling — Redwood Console will surface token-level cost and per-route latency; Jonah can export the traces for your infra team.
[07:12] Priya: how about security — audit logs and KMS? our enterprise compliance team needs proof we can integrate with their HSM.
[07:22] Maya: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; however for this POC you're on Hosted — we can show architecture diagrams and SSO/SCIM details. I'll share security pack.
[07:35] Carlos: please include SOC2 scope and retention details.
[07:40] Maya: noted.
[07:48] [Interruption - brief network glitch - 8s]
[08:00] Jonah: jumping back to experiments — I want to define PASS criteria for the stability gate: pass if failure rate <= 3% on trimmed set and no new guardrail bypasses in top-12. If borderline (3-5%), then require canary rollout with strict monitoring.
[08:25] Priya: sounds reasonable. what about scoring? we use a 0-100 quality score per prompt; can we align thresholds?
[08:33] Maya: yes. we'll create a shared CSV with prompt_id, golden_output, expected score, priority, and category.
[08:45] Carlos: a question: we had one example where the model invented an account number. that's high-severity — how do we block that?
[08:55] Jonah: guardrail layer should redact or trigger a block on PII patterns. we can add regexes and a lightweight classifier. also add an explicit reject case in the reranker.
[09:10] Liam: we need to test the latency impact of the extra guardrail checks. can we run them as async post-process with rollback?
[09:22] Maya: tradeoff. async reduces latency impact but increases window for bad output. business need will drive decision.
[09:35] Priya: for the stability gate let's run both: sync guardrail and async guardrail to measure delta.
[09:46] Jonah: yep. we'll instrument both.
[10:00] Maya: ok let's capture immediate deliverables — trimmed prompt set, 12 annotated failures, infra profile, experiments run and logs, security docs. anything else?
[10:15] Carlos: include a short runbook for rollback if pilot introduces regressions — auto-fallback to pinned model.
[10:25] Sofia: Redwood runtime supports automatic fallback policies; we'll include a suggested config.
[10:35] Maya: timeline recap: deliverables due 10/16-10/20, results review next sync Thursday 10/23 (proposed).
[10:48] Priya: Thursday works.
[10:52] Maya: ok, I'll send calendar invite.
[10:56] [Soft cross-talk, agreement]
[11:00] Jonah: quick note on data redaction — we will only export aggregated metrics and encrypted traces, raw content remains in your project bucket unless you opt-in.
[11:15] Liam: appreciated. we'll draft the IP/retention note.
[11:25] Maya: last thing — competitor note. you mentioned considering Bedrock earlier. if you test Bedrock baseline, we can include that as a neutral baseline in the test plan.
[11:40] Carlos: we might run a quick Bedrock head-to-head, yes.
[11:50] Maya: great. any other questions?
[12:00] Naomi: none from product. thanks all.
[12:05] Maya: thanks everyone, action items in chat; we'll follow up with the trimmed set and test matrix.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels occasionally generic (Speaker 1). Some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cache", "quantized" as "quantise d").
